notes: This catalog covers internationally relevant print publications outside Europe and outside the separately modeled US catalog.
Countries remain metadata on each entry; they are not separate catalog blocks and there is no requirement to represent every country.
Selection is based on international or regional relevance, reach, agenda-setting role, and viewpoint diversity. Reach is metadata, never an exclusion threshold.
Political orientation and radicality require attributed provenance; FSC does not infer orientation from country, language, party endorsements, constitutional questions, or ownership alone.
Political and radical publications may be included when relevant. Sparse viewpoints remain sparse rather than being filled by quota-driven reclassification.
Print activity must be verified; discontinued print publications are excluded or documented separately.
Party press remains an independent dimension.
Decision A applies globally to this catalog: country-specific political positions are preserved without forced FSC-axis mapping unless external provenance directly supports the FSC group assignment.

research_notes: Priority-country lists guide research only; they are not coverage requirements.
The catalog may contain several titles from a highly relevant media market and none from another country.
Candidate review is performed as one international set rather than one approval cycle per country.
Europe is excluded as a region rather than by enumerating European country codes; DE/AT/CH/GB are therefore covered transitively by the Europe exclusion.
Initial implementation size is a working guideline only and may change during candidate review.

Initial broad pool intentionally exceeds the implementation target; candidates will be reduced by current print status, international/regional relevance, provenance quality and incremental viewpoint value.
Daily Maverick is a print-status risk because its core product is digital; verify recurring physical publication before promotion.
Maclean's, The Saturday Paper, Mail & Guardian and similar non-daily titles remain eligible because the catalog covers magazines and periodicals as well as newspapers.
The first curated international shortlist contains 40 titles from 13 countries; deferred titles remain documented rather than deleted.

Turkey verification confirms that recurring print status and political descriptors can be sourced, but descriptors such as Kemalist/pro-government do not map one-to-one onto the FSC left-right taxonomy. This is a product-level cross-market comparability decision, not a data-cleaning issue.
Decision 2 requires two independent external sources before FSC political-group assignment; conflict or non-equivalent country-specific labels remain unclassified.

Decision A on control scope: state-owned, party-official, state-managed and state-funded print outlets may be included when relevant, with control metadata stored separately from political-axis classification.
International print coverage now includes active magazines/periodicals alongside newspapers; publication-form diversity is relevance-driven rather than quota-driven.
Current print activity has been verified for all 50 implemented titles using current publisher/subscription/print-edition evidence; activity status does not imply political classification.

Radical-edge assignments use the same two-independent-source rule; Green Left and Red Flag are supported by an Australian peer-reviewed fringe-left classification plus independent media-bias evidence, while Yeni Akit has two independent peer-reviewed far-right classifications.

Previously deferred candidates are reactivated when current recurring print status and material geographic, editorial or format value are verified; the former approximately-40 implementation target is not an exclusion rule.

All originally deferred candidates have now been resolved: active recurring print products are included; Daily Maverick is represented by its concrete weekly print product DM168 under the brand-as-source/print-product-as-outlet policy.
State/party control and state funding are modeled as media_positioning provenance and never used as a shortcut for FSC left-right classification.
The original approximately-40-title guideline was superseded by the resolved active candidate set and later scope expansion; the catalog remains uncapped.
Southeast Asia gap review added active print titles from Indonesia and the Philippines based on current publisher subscription/edition evidence and 2026 public procurement evidence.
Latin America gap review added current weekend print editions from Chile and Colombia; reduced print frequency is represented as weekly_newspaper rather than assuming historical daily cadence.

political_mapping_review.issue: Several internationally relevant print outlets are described by country-specific positions such as Kemalist or pro-government that are not safely equivalent to FSC's six left-right groups.

options.preserve_unmapped: Keep such titles politically unclassified on the FSC left-right axis while storing attributed media_positioning classifications.
options.force_crosswalk: Define an explicit FSC crosswalk from country-specific positions to the six global political groups, with provenance and documented caveats.

political_mapping_review.decision: Decision A plus Decision 2: country-specific political positions are not force-mapped onto FSC's six-group left-right axis, and an FSC political-group assignment requires at least two independent external sources whose descriptions materially agree on the relevant left-right direction.
political_mapping_review.provenance_policy: Attributed country-specific media_positioning may be stored separately; FSC group assignment requires external evidence that directly supports the mapped left-right category.

rules: A single media-bias database classification may be stored as attributed provenance but cannot by itself determine an FSC political group.
FSC political-group assignment requires at least two independent external sources whose descriptions materially agree on the relevant left-right direction.
Country-specific labels such as Kemalist, pro-government, constitutionalist or party-endorsement evidence do not by themselves establish an FSC left-right group.
Where sources conflict, describe different dimensions, or are too context-specific, the outlet remains politically unclassified.
No automatic mechanical crosswalk is applied solely from one provider's taxonomy.

scope_review.issue: The current 40-title shortlist omits globally influential print outlets whose editorial independence is structurally constrained by party-state ownership, state ownership, or substantial government funding. The existing source metadata model can represent this separately as media_positioning provenance without forcing it onto the FSC left-right axis.
